subject: Urban Planning
title: Desalination: Drinking the Ocean
description: A fast breakdown of Desalination: Drinking the Ocean for builders.

hook.text: Israel gets 80% of its drinking water from the Mediterranean Sea. Desalination turned a desert nation into a water exporter.

buildup.text: Reverse osmosis forces seawater through membranes, removing salt. The technology uses massive amounts of energy.

discovery.text: Israel's Sorek plant produces 150 million gallons daily — the world's largest desalination facility.

twist.text: Desalination creates toxic brine — super-salty waste water that kills marine life when dumped back in the ocean.

climax.text: As freshwater sources shrink from climate change, coastal cities from Cape Town to Chennai are turning to the sea.

punchline.text: Unlimited water source, limited energy. The ocean is free — desalting it isn't.

quiz.question: What is the main environmental concern with desalination?
options: The process releases greenhouse gases from ocean water
Toxic brine waste harms marine ecosystems when discharged
Desalination plants destroy coastal habitats during construction
